notes: Curriculum Content preserved the seven independently approved non-geometry DRAFT cards unchanged and revised only the geometry group after Independent Mathematical Review and Architecture required a 2-D/3-D split.
The three r1 combined geometry proposals are superseded DRAFT proposals, not aliases or authority; their Git history remains in r1.
Six replacement geometry labels were collision-audited against the two authoritative candidate sources on main at their pinned blob SHAs; no exact code was found.
Rectangle, square and inclusive trapezoid conventions are explicit; 3-D construction requires observable production; 2-D composition uses an unambiguous diagonal-half rectangle arrangement.
Prerequisite concepts are descriptive, not approved canonical dependency edges.
No card changes canonical UUIDs, aliases, generators, assessments, learner evidence, mastery or standards coverage.

3-D faces, curved surfaces or solid classification

shape_universe.composition_contract: Component interiors are disjoint; joining along all or part of a boundary is permitted when it produces the requested result.

inclusions: Combine two or more bounded 2-D component figures to make a specified result
Join parts without interior overlap; shared boundary contact is allowed and must be explicit
Use rotations or reflections without changing component identity
Name component parts as explanation evidence without creating additional mastery credit
exclusions: Merely identifying parts without composing them
Interior overlap when a partition is required

examples.input: Take two congruent right triangles that are exact diagonal halves of one rectangle. Join their congruent hypotenuses using a half-turn so corresponding legs are parallel; name the result and parts.
examples.answer: a rectangle composed of two congruent right triangles

examples.input: Join two congruent squares along one complete side with disjoint interiors.
examples.answer: a rectangle composed of two squares

examples.input: Place one square completely on top of another and claim a two-part rectangle.
examples.rationale: The interiors overlap, so the required non-overlapping composition was not formed.

examples.input: Name two triangles in a completed diagram without arranging them.
examples.rationale: Part identification without composition is insufficient.

misconception_probes: Counts overlapping pieces as separate parts
Changes a component name after rotation
Names only the result and omits the parts
Identifies parts without composing them
Assumes any two congruent right triangles joined along equal-length sides form a rectangle

assessment_evidence_matrix.rule: The learner must create the requested 2-D result from non-overlapping parts and explain the parts. Explanation accompanies the same attempt and creates no second credit.
prohibitions: No separate credit for naming parts
